name: Parliament House
assumptions: Main front set to bearing 238.8, not the dossier 58.8: all photos show the Kalima panel, porticos and star-parterre lawns on the south-west face.
Height is fitted, not published: roof of the central slab 29 m, wing roof 22.2 m, flag top 42 m, from a reconstructed camera on the official head-on photo.

OSM footprint is taken as the base of the upper wings; tier A steps out 8 m at the front, 10 m north-west, 4.9 m south-east and 3 m at the rear, read from the Esri plan after allowing for about 6 m of roof parallax, so each is good to about 2 to 3 m.
Rear steps are the plainest reading: the plan shows no visible terrace on the north-east side, and up to about 4 m could be hidden behind the displaced roof; no photo of the rear was found.

Slab front width 41 m from the head-on photo and the 39.6 m hall dome (the sheared Esri plan reads about 35 m, the photo was preferred); the dome itself is internal and is not modelled, as the dossier notes.
Rear and side elevations use the front's ribbon rhythm; only the front, the south-east side and the plan view were seen.
Bay counts come from the front (about 5 m pitch); side and rear counts are extrapolated.

Court plan is read from the sheared Esri view to about 3 m and is not symmetrised: each side is a front and rear well joined by a slit past the arm end, with the white L-shaped returns drawn as a plain ledge at tier B level; their true level and form, the court interiors and windows are assumed.
Slab rear is taken nearly flush with the rear wall from the plan, narrower there (about 25 m) than the front; the rear notch of the earlier model had no source.
Ground storey of tier A is drawn solid behind the retaining wall; the ribbons counted are the upper four of the five floors.
The Kalima inscription is deliberately not reproduced: a plain pale band and two rosettes stand for the lettering in the dark panel.
Exterior cladding is undocumented: white stone with a joint pattern from one close photo; colours other than the two dossier roof greys are photo estimates.
Solar panels are navy from the drone photo (the dossier's grey is a satellite reading); rows run east-west following the plan view, their number approximate; plant boxes are indicative.
Porticos, gates and canopy are public-exterior items simplified from photos; trees, flagpoles, lawns, security barriers and the forecourt are left to the world.
